chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who married a woman and stipulated upon her that he would come to her whenever he wished, and provide for her a specified amount every month. He said: 'There is no problem with it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no problem with it/permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to stipulate in a marriage contract that the husband will visit his wife only when he desires?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates a marital stipulation allowing the husband discretionary control over conjugal visits, provided he fulfills the specified monthly maintenance. This ruling highlights the flexibility within Shia jurisprudence regarding private marital agreements, emphasizing that such conditions do not void the contract as long as the core obligations of *nafaqah* (maintenance) are met. It reflects the scholarly principle that mutual consent can tailor specific aspects of marital life without contravening essential Islamic norms.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who married a woman and stipulated upon her that he would be coming to her whenever he so desires to, and he would be spending upon her a specified amount every month. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 3. Al-Husayn from Muhammad has narrated from Mu’alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from ‘Abd al- Rahman ibn abu ‘Abd Allah who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
about the case of a man who marries a woman with the condition to come to her whenever he wants and pays her an agreed upon amount every month. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful.’”
